csharp_space_after_keywords_in_control_flow_statements #

Generalized export property; sets every option it expands to at once. Measured: at false the oracle closes up all nine control-flow keywords at once — if(b), while(b), for(…), foreach(…), switch(b), catch(…), lock(o), using(…), fixed(…). ⚠ The prefixed spelling of the same generalized property is also in this export, and the pair is two registry entries naming one group rather than two spellings of one option — so OptionResolver.Expand settles the overlap by position and the oracle does the same. The earlier claim that the more specific spelling takes it was never true of Expand, whose specificity tie-break is only reachable for two assignments on one line.

Typetrue / false
Defaulttrue
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two
TierA — the formatter reads it and a committed oracle fixture pins it
Languageany
Since0.1

skala_int_align #

Generalized export property; sets every option it expands to at once. ⚠ Two recorded claims about this key are refuted, and it is measurable because of it. (1) "skala_int_align = true alone produces no alignment from the oracle" is wrong: at true the oracle pads ten of an eighteen-file probe — fields, properties, methods, locals, assignments, trailing comments, switch sections, switch-expression arms, enum initializers, chopped parameter lists. (2) "Nothing applies the expansion; OptionResolver resolves keys and aliases and leaves generalized properties alone" is stale — OptionResolver.Expand has written each generalized key's value into the keys it names since the expansion work, so Skala moves too. Both engines therefore move on constructs/alignment/int-align.cs, and the sweep's verdict there is DIVERGENT with the baseline agreeing: they agree at false (the export's value) and disagree at true, on one line. The whole divergence is an interaction inside the family — with skala_int_align_methods and skala_int_align_parameters both on, the oracle pads inside the parameter list (void Method(int a) { }) and Skala pads after the ) (void Method(int a) { }) — which neither key shows when flipped alone.

Typetrue / false
Defaultfalse
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two

Languageany
Since0.1

tab_width #

Generalized export property; sets every option it expands to at once. ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against the oracle at 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified not a formatter option. Probed at 1, 4 and 8 under indent_style = tab on a four-level tab-indented fixture, and again with skala_max_line_length = 60 so that column arithmetic decides a wrap. Flat in both engines at every value. The positive control is on the same fixture: skala_max_line_length at 120 against 40 is CONFORMANT with two distinct outputs, so the fixture's layout does depend on columns — a tab width is a display width, and one indent level is one tab whatever it counts as. skala_indent_size at 4 against 8 is likewise flat under indent_style = tab.

Typeinteger
Default4
Default known fromthe Rider export, which is Rider's default for most keys and the author's choice for the rest, with nothing distinguishing the two

Languageany
